title: AWS Lambda's Self-Managed Code Storage Lifts the Account Quota, Not the Function Size Limit
gist: AWS Lambda now lets functions and layers reference deployment packages directly in a customer-owned S3 bucket, removing the per-Region aggregate code storage quota and raising the Lambda-managed default from 75 GB to 300 GB. The widely-shared 'no storage limits' framing is misleading: per-function limits are unchanged at 50 MB zipped, 250 MB unzipped and 10 GB for container images, and the real change is that storage cost moves from an invisible Lambda quota onto the customer's own S3 bill.

themes.theme: What Actually Changed Versus the Marketing Framing

insights.claim: AWS Lambda's self-managed code storage removes the per-Region code storage quota that teams with large function fleets previously had to raise via support tickets, and raises the default Lambda-managed storage allowance from 75 GB to 300 GB.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Removes a support-ticket friction point for the largest serverless fleets, but the quantitative headroom change matters only to a small top tail of customers.
insights.locator: AWS recently announced self-managed code storage for Lambda

insights.claim: The change does not lift per-function package limits, which remain 50 MB zipped and 250 MB unzipped for zip-based functions and 10 GB for container images, so teams hitting a size wall on an individual function are in exactly the same position as before.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Shipping larger ML models inside a Lambda package is still blocked, so the constraint pushing model-serving workloads toward containers, SageMaker or Bedrock is unchanged.
insights.locator: Yet it does not change the per-function package limits

insights.claim: The announcement framing by AWS - summarized by principal serverless developer advocate Julian Wood as no storage limits, store as much function and layer code as your bucket allows - proved easy to misread, prompting the immediate community question of whether larger models could now ship inside a function package.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A case study in how cloud-vendor launch language inflates perceived capability - discount headline serverless feature claims until per-unit limits are checked.
insights.quote: no storage limits: store as much function and layer code as your bucket allows
insights.locator: Julian Wood, principal developer advocate for serverless at AWS

insights.claim: A blunt community response captured the economic reading of the change, framing it as the same limits with AWS now able to bill for storage and retrieval costs on top.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Watch whether self-managed storage converts previously bundled Lambda capacity into billable S3 revenue - a small but real monetization shift.
insights.quote: No, the same limits still apply. Now AWS can bill you for the storage and retrieval costs too.
insights.locator: The answer from another developer was blunt

insights.claim: Lambda no longer creates an intermediate copy of the deployment package when referencing customer buckets directly, which can speed up function activation after creates and updates, according to AWS Serverless Hero Darryl Ruggles.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Faster deploy-to-active time is the concrete operational win, most relevant to teams running high-frequency deployments across large function fleets.
insights.quote: With this change you can reference source code directly from your own buckets and Lambda no longer creates an intermediate copy. This can speed up function activation after creates and updates.
insights.locator: Darryl Ruggles, an AWS Serverless Hero, noted on X

insights.claim: There are no extra Lambda charges beyond standard S3 storage and any cross-Region transfer, which shifts storage cost from an invisible Lambda-side quota to a visible line item on the customer's own S3 bill.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Cost visibility moves to the customer, which enables FinOps attribution but also converts a hidden cost into a line item that cost-optimization tools can now target.
insights.locator: Ruggles added that there are no extra Lambda charges

insights.claim: The deployment workflow is unchanged because the bucket reference is resolved at update time rather than continuously, so UpdateFunctionCode must still be called after replacing the object and pointing Lambda at a bucket does not turn that bucket into a live code feed.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: No CI/CD pipeline redesign is unlocked here, which limits how much this feature can change deployment tooling behaviour.
insights.locator: The deployment workflow itself is unchanged

insights.claim: The most grounded community framing is that this is a native option overcoming the managed storage limit that most teams will never reach, alongside benefits of a single source of truth in the customer's account and visibility through existing S3 metrics and lifecycle rules.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Addressable impact is narrow - large-fleet serverless shops and governance-driven buyers - not the broad serverless base.
insights.quote: It is a native option that overcomes the managed storage limit, and most teams will never reach it.
insights.locator: Another commenter framed the value plainly

themes.theme: Infrastructure-as-Code Lag as an Adoption Brake

insights.claim: Infrastructure-as-code support is lagging: a Terraform provider enhancement request for an s3_object_storage_mode attribute on aws_lambda_function was filed on July 15 and remains open with no implementation, so Terraform-standardized teams must wait or fall back to the CLI and SDKs where the parameter is already available.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Terraform provider lag is a recurring, measurable throttle on AWS feature adoption - a useful leading indicator of when a launch actually reaches enterprise production.
insights.locator: Infrastructure-as-code support is still catching up

insights.claim: Self-managed code storage is available in all commercial AWS Regions at no additional Lambda charge, so the rollout is immediate and global rather than staged.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Universal Region availability removes the usual staged-rollout excuse, making IaC support the sole remaining adoption gate.
insights.locator: Self-managed code storage is available in all commercial AWS Regions
